gen-dafont-oldtimer-gf-science-gothic: Oldtimer's round forms curve like open parentheses, with no calligraphic swell on any downstroke. Science Gothic then lets stroke ends sit far apart, so a long passage feels like taking in one letter at a time, with no thick and thin anywhere.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-atkinson-hyperlegi: Origami looks like single-stroke sign painting, all one width. Atkinson Hyperlegible brings clipped capitals and ascenders beside its lowercase, with wide-set terminals on s, so what the pair does best is trade a brushy lead-type mass for crisp, distinct letters.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-blinker: Contemporary and a little unusual, Origami stacks its lowercase like poured lead type. Blinker then holds its lines at a steady thickness with open apertures, so a long passage goes down smoothly and clean.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-chivo: Sign-painter brush strokes, all cut to one width. Chivo packs its lowercase up toward the caps and leaves daylight in every curve, so the two sit together like a heavy painted banner over tidy, compact lines.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-geist: Unique is the mood in Origami, a single-stroke brush look with a lowercase mass like poured lead type. Geist sits next to it with a quiet, level beat and words that read as solid blocks, so the two feel like a loud sign beside a hushed whisper.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-georama: Unique, flat-lined Origami draws like a fineliner on paper and packs its lowercase into a heavy mass. And Georama does the opposite job, with a wide-open c like a bracelet pulled apart and barely rising capitals that make text easy to move through.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-gidole: Fat, brushy letters with no pressure swell at all lead here. And Gidole follows with open, scissor-blade terminals and a neon-tube consistency, so the two sit together like a sign and its quiet label.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-chorasmi: Origami draws every stroke at constant width, with no thick-thin shift between downstrokes and connecting curves. And Noto Sans Chorasmian lets curves stop short instead of closing, so a longer stretch reads with a large x-height and short ascenders.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Unique is the word for Origami, whose smooth tube-like lines excel at a solid, poured-lead mass. And Noto Sans Deseret does the quieter work, with open apertures and a high, wide-looking lowercase that keep text legible.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-devanaga: Origami has no hairlines anywhere, just brush strokes at constant width. Noto Sans Devanagari follows with an open-curved g and a compact skyline where capitals blend into lowercase, so a longer passage moves along smoothly and modern.
